en-e1-l1.title: Alphabet and di first sounds
en-e1-l1.concept: E easy to remember words when you know their first sound and first letter. Make di sounds loud as you dey read.
en-e1-l1.example: ball → B, cat → C, dog → D

en-e1-l5.title: Words for classroom
en-e1-l5.concept: desk, chair, bag, pencil, book... Talk di things for your classroom for English.

en-e1-l4.title: Family
en-e1-l4.concept: mother (mama), father (papa), grandmother (grandmama), baby (small pikin): na words for people for your family.

en-e1-l2.title: How to greet person
en-e1-l2.concept: When you meet person, talk **Hello**. When you dey leave, talk **Goodbye**. Use **My name is ...** to tell person your name.

en-e1-l3.title: Numbers and colours
en-e1-l3.concept: Learn di words for numbers like one, two, three... and di words for colours like red, blue, yellow...
en-e1-l3.example: three = 3, red = di colour of strawberry

en-e2-l3.title: I like / I have
en-e2-l3.concept: **I like ...** mean say you enjoy something. **I have ...** mean say something belong to you.
en-e2-l3.example: I like dogs. I have a cat.

en-e2-l1.title: Names of animals and things
en-e2-l1.concept: Words wey name things, like rabbit (animal with long ears), bird (animal wey dey fly) and fish (animal wey dey swim), na **nouns**.

en-e2-l5.title: Read short passages
en-e2-l5.concept: When you dey read, first find di words from di question inside di passage.

en-e4-l5.title: Read short passages
en-e4-l5.concept: Find who do wetin, and where, inside di passage, then answer.

en-e2-l4.title: Make short sentences
en-e2-l4.concept: After I, use **am**. After You, use **are**. Sentence order na: 'who → wetin di person be / wetin di person dey do'.
en-e2-l4.example: I am a student. You are kind.

en-e2-l2.title: Words wey show action
en-e2-l2.concept: Words wey show action, like jump (go up for air), run (move fast) and eat (chop food), na **verbs**.

en-e3-l1.title: Build sentences
en-e3-l1.concept: Sentence order na: 'who → does → what'. After He, She or person name, add **-s** to di verb.

en-e3-l2.title: Pronouns: words wey stand for names
en-e3-l2.concept: Instead of name, you fit use **He**, **She**, **It**, **They** or **We**.
en-e3-l2.example: Tom is tall. He is tall.

en-e3-l5.title: Understand wetin passage talk
en-e3-l5.concept: Read di passage and find who do wetin, and when.

en-e5-l5.title: Understand wetin passage talk
en-e5-l5.concept: Long passages easy more when you find who, where, when and wetin happen, as if you dey draw line under them.

en-e3-l4.title: Wetin person dey do every day
en-e3-l4.concept: get up, brush my teeth, eat breakfast, go to bed... Talk your everyday routine for English.

en-e3-l3.title: Present and past tense
en-e3-l3.concept: For things wey dey happen now or again and again, use **present tense**. For things wey don happen, use **past tense**: add **-ed** for di end of di verb.

en-e4-l3.title: Words for shape and how person feel
en-e4-l3.concept: Words like big, small, hot and cold describe how something look or feel.

en-e4-l4.title: Words for places
en-e4-l4.concept: Use **on**, **in**, **under** and **behind** to talk where things dey.
en-e4-l4.example: The book is on the desk.

en-e4-l2.title: Questions and negative sentences
en-e4-l2.concept: Start question with **Do/Does**. To make negative sentence, use **don't/doesn't**.
en-e4-l2.example: Do you like pizza? I don't like onions.

en-e4-l1.title: Present, past and future tense
en-e4-l1.concept: For now or habits, use **present tense**. For past, add **-ed**. For wetin you go do, use **will + base verb**.
en-e4-l1.example: I will visit my aunt tomorrow.

en-e5-l2.title: Words wey dey compare things
en-e5-l2.concept: To compare two things, use **-er + than**. For di one wey pass all, use **the -est**. For long words, use **more**.

en-e5-l3.title: Talk about wetin go happen
en-e5-l3.concept: For things wey you go do, use **will + base verb** or **be going to + base verb**.
en-e5-l3.example: I am going to visit Jeju.

en-e5-l1.title: Articles, plural nouns and There is/are
en-e5-l1.concept: Use **an** before vowel sound and **a** before consonant sound. For one thing, use **There is**. For plenty things, use **There are**.
en-e5-l1.example: an apple, two boxes, There are three books.

en-e5-l4.title: Write sentence another way
en-e5-l4.concept: For negative sentences, use **not / don't / doesn't / didn't**. For questions, put **Are / Do / Does** for di start of di sentence.
en-e5-l4.example: I am happy. → I am not happy.

en-e6-l4.title: Words wey join ideas
en-e6-l4.example: I was tired, so I went to bed early.

en-e6-l2.title: can, must, should, may
en-e6-l2.concept: After **can** (fit do), **must** (must do), **should** (e good make you do), **may** (you get permission), use di base form of di verb.

en-e6-l5.title: Read paragraphs
en-e6-l5.concept: Read passage wey get several sentences and find who do something, when and why.
en-e6-l5.example: Jina was tired because they walked a lot.

en-e6-l1.title: Revise all di tenses
en-e6-l1.concept: For wetin dey happen now, use **be + -ing**. For past, use **past tense**. For future, use **will / be going to**.

en-e6-l3.title: Learn more words
en-e6-l3.concept: Learn words wey get similar meaning and opposite words together, and your word knowledge go double.

en-h1-l2.title: Relative adverbs and noun clauses
en-h1-l2.concept: where / when / why na relative words wey work like adverbs. whether / that dey introduce noun clauses.
en-h1-l2.example: This is the town where I was born.

en-h1-l4.title: Linking words and how passage take flow
en-h1-l4.concept: Separate cause and effect (so, therefore), contrast (however), examples (for example) and addition (in addition).
en-h1-l4.example: However = but, on di other hand

en-h1-l5.title: Main idea and how to fill blank
en-h1-l5.concept: Di main idea often dey after However, wey dey turn common belief around, and for di last sentence. Follow problem → solution → result to fill blank.
en-h1-l5.example: problem → how to solve am → wetin happen because of am

en-h1-l3.title: Participle clauses
en-h1-l3.concept: Remove di conjunction and subject, then change di verb to -ing. Di subject must be di same for both parts.

en-h1-l1.title: Perfect and perfect continuous tenses
en-h1-l1.concept: had + p.p. na for wetin happen before another past event. have been -ing na for action wey don dey continue reach now.
en-h1-l1.example: I have been waiting for an hour.

en-h2-l1.title: Inversion and how to put emphasis
en-h2-l1.concept: When Never/Hardly/Only then come first, di order change to auxiliary + subject. Use It is ~ that for emphasis.
en-h2-l1.example: Never have I seen such a view.

en-h2-l5.title: How ideas for passage take connect
en-h2-l5.concept: Follow wetin pointing words refer to and di linking words for di passage. Join di details to reach conclusion.
en-h2-l5.example: In this way = by doing am like this

en-h2-l2.title: Subjunctive: conditions wey no be real
en-h2-l2.concept: For I wish / as if / If clauses, use past tense for wetin no true now and had p.p. for wetin no true for past.
en-h2-l2.example: I wish I had studied harder.

en-h2-l4.title: Understand word from wetin surround am
en-h2-l4.concept: Use contrast, example, cause and prefix clues to work out new word meaning.

en-h2-l3.title: Compound relatives and concession clauses
en-h2-l3.concept: whatever, whoever, whichever and however + adjective mean 'no matter wetin / who / which one / how ...'.
en-h2-l3.example: However hard it is, I will try.

en-h3-l4.title: Words wey go together and idioms
en-h3-l4.concept: Learn word pairs wey dey go together, like make a decision, take a risk and heavy rain. Use di situation to work out idiom meaning.
en-h3-l4.example: the last straw = di last problem wey make person lose patience

en-h3-l3.title: Arrange sentences and put sentence for di right place
en-h3-l3.concept: Use linking words, pointing words and time order as clues to arrange sentences and find where given sentence fit enter.
en-h3-l3.example: wetin cause am → wetin person do → result

en-h3-l1.title: Parallel structure and agreement
en-h3-l1.concept: Phrases wey and/but/or join must get di same form. Di verb must agree with di main subject.

en-h3-l5.title: Complete summary
en-h3-l5.concept: Find di main idea and expressions wey contrast for di passage, then shorten them into one sentence.
en-h3-l5.example: cost more ↔ save money in the long run

en-h3-l2.title: Mood, tone and purpose
en-h3-l2.concept: Use describing words and feeling words to find mood. Check whether passage dey ask, inform or persuade to find di purpose.
en-h3-l2.example: Please store enough water. → dey give information (notice)

en-m2-l4.title: Comparative and superlative forms
en-m2-l4.concept: -er/-est and more/most. Use than with comparatives and the with superlatives. good → better → best no follow regular rule.

en-m2-l3.title: to-infinitives and gerunds
en-m2-l3.concept: want, hope, decide + to-infinitive; enjoy, finish, avoid + gerund. stop + to V show purpose; stop + V-ing mean stop di action.
en-m2-l3.example: I want to buy a bike. She enjoys singing.

en-m2-l2.title: Passive voice
en-m2-l2.concept: Use be + past participle to show say somebody or something receive di action. Add who do di action with by.
en-m2-l2.example: The room is cleaned by Mina.

en-m2-l1.title: Present perfect tense
en-m2-l1.concept: have/has + past participle. E dey show experience, completion or continuation. Know di difference between since (particular starting time) and for (how long).
en-m2-l1.example: I have lived here for five years.

en-m2-l5.title: Reading: topic and details
en-m2-l5.concept: Read di question first, then find di sentence wey get clue. Di title and main idea cover di whole passage.
en-m2-l5.example: As a result = because of wetin happen

en-m3-l2.title: Conditionals and second conditional
en-m3-l2.concept: If + present, will + V (wetin fit happen). If + past, would + V (imagine wetin no true now).
en-m3-l2.example: If I were rich, I would travel.

en-m3-l4.title: Participles
en-m3-l4.concept: -ing dey show active or ongoing action; -ed dey show passive or finished action. For feelings, use -ing for wetin cause di feeling and -ed for di person wey feel am.
en-m3-l4.example: an exciting game / I am excited

en-m3-l3.title: Indirect questions
en-m3-l3.concept: Use question word + subject + verb order. No use do/does/did.
en-m3-l3.example: Do you know where he lives?

en-m3-l5.title: Reading: draw conclusion and find purpose
en-m3-l5.concept: Join clues to work out wetin passage no talk directly. Use requests and claims to decide di purpose of di passage.
en-m3-l5.example: Could you tell me ...? → question (to ask for information)

en-m3-l1.title: Relative pronouns
en-m3-l1.concept: Join two sentences into one with who (people), which (things), that (both) and whose (ownership).
en-m3-l1.example: I have a friend who lives in Canada.

en-l3.title: Present simple for regular verbs
en-l3.concept: When di subject na **he / she / it (third person singular)**, add **-s / -es** to di verb. Words wey end with -ch, -sh, -s, -x, -o take -es. For consonant + y, change y to i and add -es!
en-l3.example: go → goes / watch → watches / study → studies

en-e3-abc1.title: Capital letters and small letters
en-e3-abc1.concept: Alphabet get **capital letters** and **small letters**. Many pairs look different, so learn one pair at a time. Take care with letters wey look alike, like b, d, p and q.

en-e3-snd1.title: Sounds and spelling
en-e3-snd1.concept: Di first sound of word connect with di first letter. Find words wey start with di same sound to learn how sound and spelling connect. Sometimes two letters, like ph, dey make di f sound.

en-e6-seq1.title: Find di order wey events happen
en-e6-seq1.concept: Words wey show order, like **First**, **Then / Next**, **After that** and **Finally**, show di order wey things take happen.
en-e6-seq1.example: First, I wake up. Then I eat breakfast. Finally, I go to school.

en-e6-pun1.title: Capital letters and punctuation
en-e6-pun1.concept: Start sentence with **capital letter** and end am with di right **punctuation mark**: period (.) for statement, question mark (?) for question, exclamation mark (!) for surprise or strong feeling. Person names and di word I must always start with capital letter.
en-e6-pun1.example: Is this your bag? Yes, it is.

en-m2-sum1.title: Summarise passage
en-m2-sum1.concept: To summarise, find di **main idea** and reduce am to one or two sentences. Sentence wey talk only one detail, add wetin no dey for passage, or cover too much no be good summary.
en-m2-sum1.example: Recycling saves resources and reduces trash.

en-l1.title: Learn everyday words
en-l1.concept: Learn common words with **sound + meaning + spelling** together so you go remember them for long. Tap di speaker button to hear their sounds.
en-l1.example: library = place wey person fit borrow books / desk = table for work / milk = white drink from cow

en-l2.title: Di verb be: am / are / is
en-l2.concept: Di verb be dey change with di subject. **I → am**, **he / she / it → is**, **you / we / they → are**.
en-l2.example: I am a student. She is my friend. They are in the classroom.

en-l4.title: Plural nouns and how to build sentences
en-l4.concept: For two or more, normally add **-s** to di noun. Nouns wey end with -x take **-es**. Memorise irregular plurals. Sentence order na **subject → verb → di rest**.
en-l4.example: book → books / box → boxes / child → children

en-h3e-l1.title: Choose wetin fit di situation
en-h3e-l1.concept: For conversation questions, no check grammar alone: check whether di tone natural and polite for di situation. Offers, interrupting, answering compliments, idioms and indirect speech dey show often.

en-h3e-l2.title: Workplace expressions and words wey go together
en-h3e-l2.concept: For workplace English, important points na idioms (touch base), short forms (ASAP, etc.) and verb-preposition pairs (collocations). No translate word by word; learn them as groups wey people dey use for work.

en-h3e-l3.title: Read information with careful reasoning
en-h3e-l3.concept: For media English, e important to separate facts from opinions and check whether claim get good reasoning. Learn terms for image descriptions (alt text, caption) and editing tools by wetin dem dey do.

en-h3e-l4.title: Culture words and open mind
en-h3e-l4.concept: For world culture topics, learn words like culture, diversity and stereotype, and how to understand other cultures without judging them. Use context clues to separate words wey look alike.

en-h3e-l5.title: Read stories with literature terms
en-h3e-l5.concept: For literature questions, know wetin term mean and apply am to di scene for di story. Separate foreshadowing, symbol, point of view, theme and character roles.

en-h3e-l6.title: Separate arguments and faulty reasoning
en-h3e-l6.concept: For debate, separate terms (motion, rebuttal, etc.), kinds of evidence and errors for reasoning. When you dey judge claim, first ask, "Wetin be di evidence for this?"

en-h3e-l7.title: Write accurately for di right purpose
en-h3e-l7.concept: For writing, choose di form wey fit di purpose and reader. Check sentence parts (subject and verb) and whether linking words make sense. For text like resume, use clear actions and numbers instead of vague words.
